title: Groundwater Audit
question: Did arsenic and nitrate decline at repeatedly sampled wells in San Bernardino County, 2000 to 2023, and where does an LLM help or quietly err in answering?
one_liner: A checked reference analysis of public USGS groundwater chemistry paired with 24 bounded, scored runs of a language model on six frozen tasks under two prompting conditions.

headline.label: Nitrate cohort wells sampled in both periods
Arsenic cohort: median late/early ratio among detected pairs

finding: The pooled nitrate median fell from {{nitrate_as_n.pooled_vs_cohort.pooled_early.km_median:.2f}} to {{nitrate_as_n.pooled_vs_cohort.pooled_late.km_median:.2f}} mg/L as N and the pooled arsenic median rose from {{arsenic.pooled_vs_cohort.pooled_early.km_median:.1f}} to {{arsenic.pooled_vs_cohort.pooled_late.km_median:.1f}} µg/L between 2000 to 2011 and 2012 to 2023. Neither is a change at wells. The late period sampled different wells, and only a minority of wells appear in both periods.

At the {{nitrate_as_n.paired_change.n_pairs}} nitrate wells sampled in both periods, {{nitrate_as_n.paired_change.decline}} declined and {{nitrate_as_n.paired_change.increase}} increased. At the {{arsenic.paired_change.n_pairs}} arsenic cohort wells, {{arsenic.paired_change.decline}} declined and {{arsenic.paired_change.increase}} increased with {{arsenic.paired_change.indeterminate}} indeterminate because of non-detects; the sign test gives p = {{arsenic.paired_change.sign_test.p_two_sided:.3f}}, but the median within-well ratio of {{arsenic.paired_change.wilcoxon_both_detected.median_ratio_late_over_early:.3f}} is a change of about 3 percent, inside the replicate precision of the measurements and coincident with a laboratory change and a ten-fold drop in reporting limit.

The evaluation ran one model on six frozen tasks under a neutral prompt and a structured-workflow prompt, two repetitions each, scored mechanically against the reference and then read against a rubric. Every run handled the four data traps. The structured workflow cost 30 percent more and did not reduce errors; the failures that did occur were definitional and were caught by reading answers against the reference definitions, not by the row counts.

traps.how: Pooled period medians moved in opposite directions for the two constituents, and neither reflected change at wells; the consistent cohort told a different story.
Arsenic reporting limits fell from about 2 to 0.1 µg/L across the record; non-detects were treated as intervals and the median estimated by Kaplan-Meier, never substituted.
Every nitrate sample appeared twice, as N and as NO3, and nitrate-plus-nitrite was stored under its own name; pooling without reconciling definitions doubles the count.

Two model runs volunteered unrequested cohort analyses on the same wells that pointed in opposite directions because of unstated weighting; both numbers reproduce and neither run said why they differ.

figures.caption: Period medians for all samples, one per well, and the consistent cohort. The pooled bars move; the cohort bars barely do.
Same well, early period against late period. Nitrate scatters around the diagonal; arsenic leans slightly below it.
Reporting limits of non-detects over time by laboratory. The arsenic limit drops an order of magnitude when the laboratory changes.
Sampling coverage by year. Effort is uneven and the late period is thin.

not_claimed: No remediation effect, aquifer-wide improvement or health conclusion.
No human time saved; no analyst session was timed.
Two repetitions per cell are not evidence of broad superiority of either prompting condition.
data: Water Quality Portal, USGS NWIS records, San Bernardino County wells, arsenic and nitrate, 2000 to 2023
